item.title: SUPER BOWL LX: ‘Dark Side’ defense leads Seahawks over Patriots
item.description: SANTA CLARA, Calif. — Defense won this championship. Devon Witherspoon, Derick Hall, Byron Murphy and the rest of Mike Macdonald’s ferocious unit pummeled Drake Maye, and the Seattle Seahawks beat the New England Patriots, 29-13, on Sunday to win the franchise’s second Super Bowl. Sam Darnold threw a touchdown pass to AJ Barner, Kenneth Walker III ran for 135 yards and Jason Myers set a Super Bowl record by making all five of his field-goal tries. item.title: CHOP Out Hunger receives $15,000 grant
item.description: CHOP Out Hunger received a $15,000 grant from the Robert and Rose Cavanaugh Fund to Feed the Hungry Poor, a charitable fund of the Scranton Area Community Foundation. The investment supports CHOP Out Hunger’s Backpack and In-School Pantry programs, which provide consistent access to nutritious food for children in Scranton and throughout Lackawanna County. item.title: COUNTERPOINT: Trump’s flawed import tariff policy
item.description: It has been 10 months since President Donald Trump’s “Liberation Day” import tariff announcement in April. Ultimately, that announcement led to U.S. import tariffs rising to an average of 17 percent, their highest level in 100 years.

item.title: BOYS BASKETBALL: Elk Lake and Susquehanna to battle in an important Division III game
item.description: Division races are coming down to the wire in Lackawanna League boys basketball. Elk Lake (18-2, 11-1) plays at Susquehanna (16-4, 11-1) on Monday at 6:45 p.m. in the most important matchup of the league season in Division III. The winner of that matchup will secure a tie for the title with one game remaining. In the first meeting, Elk Lake defeated the Sabers, 72-51, when John Heitsman and Chase Pond each scored 23 points.
